# action.docker_container_export

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Writes a container's filesystem to a local tar file, like `docker export`. The file is written next to its final name and renamed into place, so a failed export never leaves a partial tar at `path`.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_export.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_container_export" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_container_export.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_export.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `container` | `string` | required |  |  | Name or ID of the container (running or stopped). |
| `path` | `string` | required |  |  | Local file to write, on the machine running Terraform. Parent directories are created; an existing file is replaced. `~` expands to the home directory. |

## Example

```terraform
resource "docker_container" "build" {
  name    = "rootfs-build"
  image   = "alpine:3.20"
  command = ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl && sleep infinity"]

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_container_export.rootfs]
    }
  }
}

# Writes the container filesystem to a local tar. On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_export.rootfs
action "docker_container_export" "rootfs" {
  config {
    container = docker_container.build.id
    path      = "${path.module}/out/rootfs.tar"
  }
}
```
